findings.text: Fixture setup groups several primitive families under a shared class label and provides paired instances per class, with an additional real time mutex family initialized when a conditional build option is present.

Interrupt context helpers pair local masking changes with checker entry and exit notifications and assert expected context after entry, covering both hard and soft contexts with distinct disable and enable paths.

Shorthand families bind generic acquire, release, combined acquire release, and initialization operations to named fixture objects across spin, read write spin, sleeping mutex, real time mutex, and semaphore primitives.

Write wait acquisition helpers manage a lifecycle of initialization, completion, and finalization around lock, trylock, and unlock operations against a shared tracking object, with one build variant additionally arming a deadlock injection counter.
Ordered two party nesting is used as a reusable building block for larger circular wait encodings.
Case generators emit a single routine and exhaustive orderings for two and three abstract events, allowing order dependent checking behavior to be exercised without duplicating case logic.

Repeated acquisition expectations distinguish read recursive spin behavior, where nested reads on same or sibling instances are accepted, from semaphore and mixed read write nesting, which are treated as checker failures.

Ordered nesting cycles contrast safe read only interleavings with write involved reversals flagged as failures, including a chain cache variant where an intermediate safe nesting precedes a failing write nesting.

Abstract cycle encodings express circular waits across two to four generic participants and two misuse patterns involving duplicate release and initialization while held, each annotated with expected checker outcome.
Duplicate release preparation is configuration dependent, with one build quiescing scheduling migration and read side protection before the faulting releases while the other performs no preparation.

Interrupt safety suites progress from basic context comparison through enable while held, safe holder acquiring unsafe, late conversion to safe after unsafe, read write inversion, and read recursion cases split into safe and unsafe forms, expanded across hard and soft contexts and all event orders.
A reset operation returns the whole fixture set and checker tracking to a deterministic baseline so successive cases start from equivalent state.

A single case runner records total, success, expected failure, and unexpected failure tallies by comparing checker state to the declared expectation, then restores execution context protections before the next case.
A configuration gated alias either forwards real time cases to the common runner or discards them, allowing the same case list to compile in both configurations.

Cases intentionally drive the checker into failure and may disturb preemption, migration, read side nesting, or soft interrupt accounting, so the harness preserves and restores that state around each case.
